title: Silver tetradrachm, 2021.40.80
author: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
scope: The 440–404 BCE catalog range, Athena/owl design, 24 mm diameter, and public-domain images.
note: The record identifies the museum specimen shown. Its date is a catalogue attribution, not an inscribed year.

title: Athenian Tetradrachm, 1920.267
author: Cleveland Museum of Art
scope: The museum’s 480–449 BCE dating, 17.237 g weight, and linked obverse (1920.267.a) and reverse (1920.267.b) records for the same coin.
note: The current museum range is used instead of a single-year field in the older Commons import. Both side records explicitly identify 1920.267 as their parent accession and are designated CC0.

title: Tetradrachm: Head of Athena, 1941.296.a
author: Cleveland Museum of Art
scope: A 449–440 BCE specimen; 17.2 g, 23 mm; Gift of Dr. Jacob Hirsch.
note: A single measured specimen is not a universal specification for all owls.

title: Athenian tetradrachm
author: Acropolis Museum
scope: The ΑΘΕ ethnic, olive twig, owl, and incuse square; the Acropolis hoard of 1886.

title: About the ancient city of Athens and its surrounding region, Attica
author: Attic Inscriptions Online
scope: The geographical distinction between Athens and Attica.

title: Tyrants, democrats and the first silver ‘owl’ coins of Athens
author: Gillan Davis, Janne Blichert-Toft, Liesel Gentelli & Francis Albarède
scope: Archaic silver sources; chronology of the Laurion discovery; evidence against a simple one-event origin story.
note: Archaeological and Anthropological Sciences 17, 122. New analyses of 52 archaic coins plus 12 legacy measurements; the authors’ interpretation is identified as such.

title: The Reminting of Athenian Silver Coinage, 353 B.C.
author: John H. Kroll
scope: Pi-style, folded flans, reminting, and the proposed 353 BCE fiscal context.
note: Hesperia 80(2), 229–259. Consulted in the author’s online copy. Later work revisits the date; this atlas does not treat 353 as settled.

title: Athenian Tetradrachm Coinage of the First Half of the Fourth Century BC
author: John H. Kroll
scope: Early fourth-century profile-eye coinage, surviving hoards, and reminting as an explanation for rarity.
note: Revue belge de Numismatique 157, 3–26. Relative classification is more secure than every absolute date.

title: When is an owl not an owl? An analysis of Attic tetradrachms circulating in the southern Levant in the late fifth and fourth centuries BCE
author: Liesel Gentelli, Gillan Davis, Francis Albarède, Janne Blichert-Toft & Haim Gitler
scope: Three-quarter-eye owls, contested “Eastern imitation” attributions, the 404 BCE endpoint, and revised Pi-style discussion.
note: Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports 70, 105634. Consulted via the author’s full-text copy on ResearchGate. The paper reports 22 sampled coins; the atlas avoids converting a sample-specific argument into a universal authentication rule.

title: Law on approvers (dokimastai) of silver coinage, 375/4 BC (AIO 819 / RO 25)
author: Translation: Stephen Lambert & P. J. Rhodes; Attic Inscriptions Online
scope: Official testing, foreign owl-type silver, and bronze- or lead-cored coins.
note: The restored wording of the foreign-coin clause is uncertain. Its treatment of good foreign silver is not equated here with a blanket legal-tender rule.

title: Sale of confiscated property and mine leases, 367/6 BC (RO 36)
author: Attic Inscriptions Online
scope: Documentary evidence for the mining landscape of Laurion and Sounion.

title: Payments from the treasury of Athena, 410/9 BC (IG I³ 375)
author: Attic Inscriptions Online
scope: Treasury payments in talents, drachmas, and fractions of obols for civic, religious, and military purposes.

title: Sabaces Egypt van Alfen 2002 V: “Sabakes”, Athenian imitations
author: IRIS / Online Greek Coinage
scope: A securely attributed non-Athenian branch: Egyptian Athena/owl issues under Persian administration, c. 340–333 BCE.
note: The authority, coin type, and date range are distinct from the findspot of an individual coin.

title: The Chronology of the New Style Coinage of Athens
author: Otto Mørkholm
scope: Specialist chronological debate and the revision of the older New Style chronology.
note: American Numismatic Society Museum Notes 29, 29–42. Bibliographic record verified; not represented as an independently rechecked die corpus.

title: The Chronology of the Athenian New Style Coinage
author: D. M. Lewis
scope: Foundational revision of Margaret Thompson’s absolute chronology.
note: Numismatic Chronicle, 275–300. Listed as a specialist research route; full text was not independently rechecked for this edition.

title: Greece: national sides of euro coins
author: European Central Bank
scope: The Greek €1 national side adapts the owl from a fifth-century Athenian four-drachma coin.

title: Greek Silver Tetradrachm of Athens (Attica)
author: Exekias / Wikimedia Commons
scope: An archaic Athena/owl specimen, 17.09 g, cataloged c. 520–510 BCE; Seltman 302d.
note: Use the early date as the source’s attribution, not a precise mint year. CC BY 2.0, confirmed by the Commons Flickr review.

title: Sg2537: Athenian profile-eye tetradrachm
author: Classical Numismatic Group / Wikimedia Commons
scope: Paired obverse/reverse of a specimen cataloged c. 393–355 BCE; 17.12 g; SNG München 90.
note: The source image is only 500 × 253 pixels. It is labeled as a reference-quality plate, not high-resolution evidence.

title: Silver tetradrachm, Athens New Style (reverse)
author: Marie-Lan Nguyen / Wikimedia Commons; Musée de la BnF
scope: The amphora, surrounding wreath, and reverse inscriptions visible on a New Style example.
note: The file description retains an old c. 200–150 BCE attribution. That metadata is preserved in the credit, not silently adopted as this atlas’s series chronology.

title: New Style Athenian Tetradrachms, 166/164–63/62 BC
author: Forum Ancient Coins, NumisWiki
scope: One explicit alternative to the commonly encountered c. 165–42 BCE series envelope.
note: An annotated commercial reference, not a peer-reviewed authority. Used only to demonstrate divergent catalog date conventions.

title: NGC Ancients: The Elusive “Full Crest” Owls of Athens
author: NGC Ancients
scope: The conventional mass-issue range, its 404 BCE historical endpoint, and the main stylistic divisions.
note: A specialist overview is not a substitute for a die study. Any disputed absolute boundaries are marked separately.

title: Athenian silver tetradrachm, Pi III · 1966.453.1475
author: Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Monnaies, médailles et antiques
scope: Explicit identification as Pi III; accession 1966.453.1475; SNG France 1, Collection Jean et Marie Delepierre, no. 1475; weight 17.19 g and diameter 21 mm. Catalogue date: c. 353–295 BCE (BnF catalogue, attributed there to Flament). Gallica photographs are tied to this object record.
note: This is the specimen catalogue’s date range, not an exact issue date and not a claim that all Pi-style chronology is settled. Photograph rights are recorded separately on the individual Commons pages and in BnF’s reuse policy. Institutional attribution does not by itself settle image reuse rights.

title: Athenian silver tetradrachm, Quadridigité · 1966.453.1478
author: Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Monnaies, médailles et antiques
scope: Explicit identification as Quadridigité; accession 1966.453.1478; SNG France 1, Collection Jean et Marie Delepierre, no. 1478; weight 17.22 g and diameter 21 mm. Catalogue date: c. 286–261 BCE (BnF catalogue, attributed there to Flament). Gallica photographs are tied to this object record.
note: The source’s date convention is preserved. Other specialist catalogues may draw different endpoints. Photograph rights are recorded separately on the individual Commons pages and in BnF’s reuse policy. Institutional attribution does not by itself settle image reuse rights.

title: Athenian silver tetradrachm, Pi II · 1966.453.1469
author: Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Monnaies, médailles et antiques
scope: Explicit identification as Pi II; accession 1966.453.1469; SNG France 1, Collection Jean et Marie Delepierre, no. 1469; weight 17.16 g and diameter 23 mm. Catalogue date: c. 393–295 BCE (broad BnF catalogue range, attributed there to Flament). Gallica photographs are tied to this object record.
note: Do not silently turn the broad 393–295 BCE record range into the date of Pi II as a whole. The type identification and the chronology should be stored separately. Photograph rights are recorded separately on the individual Commons pages and in BnF’s reuse policy. Institutional attribution does not by itself settle image reuse rights.

title: Athens, Pi-style · Flament 2007 type record
author: IRIS / University of Oxford
scope: Type-level reference for Pi-style Athenian tetradrachms. Links the museum specimen evidence to a wider numismatic classification.
note: A type-level record is not a precise date for each photographed specimen; the BnF accession records remain the direct evidence for Pi II and Pi III identifications.

title: Athens, quadridigité · Nicolet-Pierre and Kroll 1990, nos. 1–28
author: IRIS / University of Oxford
scope: Quadridigité type entry linking the BnF specimen 1966.453.1478 to the specialist classification.
note: Quadridigité illustrates one later Old Style group; it is not a generic name for every third-century Athenian owl.

title: Heterogeneous Group C tetradrachm · Electronic Auction 594, lot 66
author: Classical Numismatic Group, Inc.
scope: Catalogues a 17.13 g, 24.5 mm coin as Heterogeneous Group C, c. 280/67–229 BCE, with a reference to Nicolet-Pierre and Kroll, Group C, no. 1 (same dies).
note: “Same dies” is the auctioneer’s die-match attribution, not a statement that this is the same physical specimen as the published reference. Only a 500 × 240 px paired preview was located. No image from this lot is embedded in the atlas; a higher-resolution original and reuse review remain outstanding.

title: Commander une reproduction avec une utilisation commerciale
author: Bibliothèque nationale de France
scope: BnF’s published conditions for commercial and promotional reuse of reproductions, with stated exceptions. Preserved alongside the individual Commons PD-France assertions.
